questions.prompt: Unknown USB drive left in a parking lot — vector?
questions.explanation: A removable device can introduce malware or remove data while bypassing network defenses.

questions.prompt: Malicious script embedded in an SVG image — vector?
questions.explanation: SY0-701 names image-based delivery as its own threat-vector category.

questions.prompt: Malicious macro inside an Office document — vector?
questions.explanation: The malicious content is delivered in a file that the target opens.

questions.prompt: Phishing link delivered by email — delivery vector?
questions.explanation: Email, SMS, and instant messaging are the three message-based examples in objective 2.2.

questions.prompt: Smishing link delivered by SMS — delivery vector?
questions.explanation: Smishing is social engineering delivered through the message-based SMS channel.

questions.prompt: Malicious link sent through Slack or instant messaging — delivery vector?
questions.explanation: Instant messaging is a message-based threat vector.

questions.prompt: Phishing lure sent in a social-media direct message — delivery vector?
questions.explanation: The delivery channel is a message even though the service is social media.

questions.prompt: Fake help-desk phone call asking for a password — vector?
questions.explanation: Vishing is social engineering delivered through a voice-call vector.

questions.prompt: Attacker exploits an unpatched browser flaw — vector?
questions.explanation: The attacker reaches the system through an exploitable flaw in client software.

questions.prompt: End-of-life operating system no longer receives fixes — vector?
questions.explanation: Unsupported products accumulate known flaws because the vendor no longer provides security fixes.

questions.prompt: Evil-twin access point at a cafe — vector?
questions.explanation: The attacker uses an untrusted wireless network path.

questions.prompt: Unprotected network jack in a public lobby — vector?
questions.explanation: Unsecure networks include wired, wireless, and Bluetooth paths.

questions.prompt: Unauthorized Bluetooth pairing attack — vector?
questions.explanation: CompTIA lists Bluetooth beneath unsecure networks.

questions.prompt: Internet-facing Telnet service left enabled — vector?
questions.explanation: An unnecessary listening service increases the reachable attack surface.

questions.prompt: Network device still uses admin/admin — vector?
questions.explanation: Vendor defaults are widely known and can provide immediate unauthorized access.

questions.prompt: Trusted software update is compromised at the vendor — vector?
questions.explanation: The attacker abuses trust in an upstream vendor or supplier.

questions.prompt: Managed service provider breach reaches its customers — vector?
questions.explanation: SY0-701 explicitly lists managed service providers under supply-chain vectors.

questions.prompt: Fraudulent message tricks a user into revealing credentials — human technique?
questions.explanation: Phishing is the broad social-engineering attempt; smishing and vishing specify delivery channels.

questions.prompt: Impersonated executive requests an urgent wire transfer — human technique?
questions.explanation: BEC impersonates a trusted business identity to induce a fraudulent action.

questions.prompt: Attacker invents a believable story to obtain information — human technique?
questions.explanation: The fabricated scenario or identity is the pretext.

questions.prompt: Attacker compromises a website frequently used by the target group — human technique?
questions.explanation: A watering-hole attack waits at a site the intended targets already trust and visit.

questions.prompt: Fake login page copies a bank’s logo and design — human technique?
questions.explanation: The attacker copies a trusted brand to make the lure appear legitimate.

questions.prompt: Attacker registers paypa1.com to catch mistyped visits — human technique?
questions.explanation: A look-alike domain exploits typing mistakes or a quick visual check.

questions.prompt: False information is deliberately spread to manipulate people — human technique?
questions.explanation: Disinformation is intentionally false; misinformation may be shared without intent to deceive.
